postmortem.what_happened: J064 was the C08 mechanical long euro from the 51% forecast of 24 Nov. It filled at the ECB reference rate of 1.0935 on 25 Nov and closed at 1.0975 on 26 Nov when the 25 Nov review flipped the forecast to 49%, netting about +0.01% of the account after costs. The euro rose about 0.4% over the day as the dollar paused before Thanksgiving and the ECB's October minutes, released on 26 Nov, showed a tightening bias.
postmortem.assessment: The thesis was a 20-trading-day call, and the position lived one day, so it was never tested; the small gain is noise. The decision process is the issue: a one-point forecast flip from 51 to 49 closed and reversed the position, paying round-trip costs that consumed over half of the gross gain, on a change of view that was within the forecaster's own noise. The mechanical rules did exactly what they say; the cost came from forecasts oscillating either side of 50.
postmortem.do_differently: Do not flip a 51/49 forecast across 50 on a single day's news or an Opposition point unless the evidence genuinely changed; a one-point view change that crosses 50 costs a full round trip. Treat 49 vs 51 as a deliberate side choice and keep it stable unless something material happens. Note for Ethan: C08's 25% no-trade band does not damp side flips near 50, which is a design question worth reviewing.
